2. The arbitrary-schedule, general-GKLS patch compiler

This is the main new computational operation.

Consider a connected patch of $N$ qubits with fixed range, arity, incidence and local GKLS strength bound. Its generator may contain arbitrary supplied piecewise-constant Hamiltonians and general nonunital local GKLS terms. No invariant state is needed.

For any fixed time and precision exponents, suppose
$\tau_{\mathrm{patch}}\le C_1\log^{c_1}(2N),
\qquad
\log(1/\delta)\le C_2N\log^{c_2}(2N).$
There is a deterministic finite-bit construction of a rational Hermiticity-preserving, trace-preserving linear-map MPO $\Upsilon$ with
$\|\Upsilon-\Phi(\tau_{\mathrm{patch}},0)\|_\diamond\le\delta$
and work
$\boxed{
\operatorname{poly}_{\mathrm{class}}(B,N)\,
\exp\!\left[
C_{\mathrm{class}}N^{11/12}\log^{c_{\mathrm{class}}}(2N)
\right].
}
\tag{1}$
The map need not be completely positive. It is a numerical approximation, and Section 3 gives its certified generative use.

The source supplies the arbitrary-drive Liouville rank certificate and the coefficient-compression machinery. Its structured-time construction explicitly distinguishes arithmetic work from finite-precision complexity and retains temporal-description overhead. The balanced construction here supplies the additional algorithm and bit accounting. arxiv.org <https://arxiv.org/html/2609.27497v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com>


Static leaves, followed by balanced composition

The accepted tilted slicing gives $O(N)$ layers with maximal width
$w=O(N^{3/4}).$
A fixed amount of blocking handles the prescribed physical range. The actual layer dimensions, exponential in $w$, are included in the cost.

Split every constant-generator interval longer than one unit of normalized time into intervals of duration at most one. If the supplied schedule has $S$ segments, the resulting leaf count satisfies
$K\le S+\lceil\tau_{\mathrm{patch}}\rceil.$
Each leaf is computed with the accepted static rational coefficient-MPO operation. Its extension to complete local GKLS terms is algebraic:


- nonnegative coupling parameters preserve the GKLS property of the deleted backgrounds;
- those backgrounds provide the CPTP contraction used in the Taylor remainder;
- fixed arity bounds each microscopic crossing rank;
- the accepted exact rational gauge argument pays coefficient heights and elimination.
